Ramon Duarte Datasheet as part of Pressure Pad Subsystem for Team 203

Submission: 10, 30, 2026

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This datasheet documents the design and development of the pressure pad subsystem for the team project. The purpose of the pressure pad subsystem is to detect when pressure is applied to the pad and provide a signal that can be processed by the microcontroller.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
The team project consists of the development of an interactive cat toy. My portion of the project is the pressure pad subsystem, which is responsible for detecting when the cat applies pressure to the pad.

More information about the complete team project can be found on the Team 203 Project Website.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
My contribution to the team project is the design and development of the pressure pad subsystem. This subsystem is incharge of detecting when there is pressure applied on the sensor, it sends a signal to the microcontroler to power on the whole system.

The complete design and documentation of my pressure pad subsystem can be found in the following sections:

  • Block Diagram
  • Component Selection
  • Bill of Materials
  • Schematic
  • Power Budget

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This block Diagram illustrates the system and how it is connected. It shows what is needed in order for the system to function for example, the input voltage from the voltage regulator as well as how the Pressure pad and other sub-systems like the onboard LED and push-button are connected to the Curiosity Nano board. Finally it illustrates how the system will communicate with the other systems in the project by showing which pins are being used.

docs.title: Pressure Sensor
docs.text:
Table 1: Pressure Sensor Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1FSR01CEOhmite Force Sensing ResistorDigiKey Product Page * Large sensing area is well suited for the pressure pad. Thin construction makes it easy to install under the pressure surface. Resistance output can be converted to voltage using a simple voltage divider. Requires relatively little supporting circuitry. Simple analog output is easy to interface with the signal-conditioning circuit. * Resistance-to-force relationship is nonlinear. Less accurate than precision force sensors such as load cells. Output can vary depending on how force is distributed across the sensing area.* Calibration is required for accurate force measurements. Option 2FSR02CEOhmite Force Sensing ResistorDigiKey Product Page * Compact size requires little installation space. Thin construction simplifies mechanical integration. Resistance output allows simple analog signal conditioning.* Requires few supporting electrical components. * Smaller sensing area is less suitable for the pressure pad. Force must be concentrated over a smaller area. Resistance-to-force relationship is nonlinear.* Requires calibration for accurate force measurements. Option 3FSR03CEOhmite Force Sensing ResistorDigiKey Product Page * Larger sensing area than the FSR02CE. Thin construction allows installation underneath the pressure surface. Resistance output is easy to interface with analog circuitry.* Requires relatively few supporting components. * Sensing area is smaller than the FSR01CE. Nonlinear response makes precise force measurements difficult. Requires calibration for quantitative measurements.* Output can vary with force distribution.

Choice: Option 1: FSR01CE

Rationale: The FSR01CE was selected because its larger sensing area is better suited for the pressure-pad subsystem. Its resistance-based output can be converted into a voltage using a simple voltage divider and conditioned before being measured by the microcontroller. The subsystem primarily needs to detect changes in applied pressure rather than make precision force measurements, making the FSR01CE a suitable combination of sensing area, simple interfacing, and mechanical integration.

docs.title: Operational Amplifier
docs.text:
Table 2: Operational Amplifier Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1MCP6004-I/PMicrochip TechnologyQuad Operational Amplifier14-PDIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Operates from 1.8 V to 6 V and is compatible with the 5 V rail. Rail-to-rail output provides a large usable output-voltage range. Four operational amplifiers are included in one IC. Low supply current reduces system power consumption. Through-hole PDIP package is easy to solder.* Extra amplifier channels allow future expansion. * 1 MHz gain-bandwidth product is lower than higher-performance alternatives. Four amplifier channels may be more than currently required. 14-pin package occupies more PCB space than an 8-pin dual amplifier.* Cannot operate directly from supply voltages greater than 6 V. Option 2MCP6002-I/PMicrochip TechnologyDual Operational Amplifier8-PDIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Operates from 1.8 V to 6 V and is compatible with the 5 V rail. Rail-to-rail output is suitable for interfacing with the microcontroller ADC. Smaller 8-pin package requires less PCB space. Low supply current reduces system power consumption. Through-hole package simplifies soldering and assembly. * Contains only two amplifier channels compared with four in the MCP6004. Future expansion could require an additional IC. 1 MHz bandwidth is lower than higher-performance alternatives.* Provides fewer amplifier channels while offering similar electrical performance to the MCP6004. Option 3TLV2464INTexas InstrumentsQuad Operational Amplifier14-PDIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Contains four operational amplifiers in one package. Compatible with the 5 V power rail. Rail-to-rail output provides a large usable output range. 6.4 MHz bandwidth provides greater performance than the MCP6004. Through-hole package simplifies manual PCB assembly. * More expensive than the MCP6004 and MCP6002. Higher supply current increases system power consumption. Additional bandwidth is unnecessary for the slowly changing pressure-pad signal.* 14-pin package provides no PCB-space advantage over the MCP6004.

Choice: Option 1: MCP6004-I/P

Rationale: The MCP6004-I/P was selected because it provides four operational amplifiers, rail-to-rail output, low power consumption, and direct compatibility with the 5 V power rail. The MCP6002-I/P requires less PCB space but only provides two amplifier channels. The TLV2464IN provides greater bandwidth, but this additional performance is unnecessary for the relatively slow pressure-pad signal. The MCP6004-I/P therefore provides the required performance while also providing additional amplifier channels for future signal-conditioning requirements.

docs.title: 5 V Voltage Regulator
docs.text:
Table 3: Voltage Regulator Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1MC7805CTGonsemi5 V Linear Voltage RegulatorTO-220 Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Provides the regulated 5 V output required by the subsystem. Through-hole TO-220 package simplifies manual soldering. High output-current capability provides substantial current margin. Common regulator architecture simplifies circuit implementation. Internal protection features improve reliability. * Excess input voltage is dissipated as heat. Requires an input voltage sufficiently above 5 V to maintain regulation. Efficiency decreases as the difference between input and output voltage increases.* Thermal management may be required at high load currents. Option 2UA7805CKCSTexas Instruments5 V Linear Voltage RegulatorTO-220 Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Fixed 5 V output directly matches the required power rail. High output-current capability provides significant design margin. Internal thermal protection improves reliability. Internal current limiting provides protection during fault conditions. Through-hole TO-220 package simplifies assembly. * Linear regulation dissipates excess input voltage as heat. Input voltage must remain sufficiently above 5 V. Current capability is much greater than required by this subsystem.* Less efficient than a switching regulator when operating from a higher input voltage. Option 3LM2931T-5.0/NOPBTexas Instruments5 V Low-Dropout Linear RegulatorTO-220 Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Fixed 5 V output matches the required system voltage. Low-dropout design can operate with a lower input voltage than conventional 7805 regulators. Through-hole TO-220 package simplifies manual soldering.* Lower dropout can reduce wasted voltage when the input supply is close to 5 V. * Lower maximum output current than the 7805 alternatives. Provides less current margin for future expansion. Still dissipates excess input voltage as heat.* Output-current capability must be verified using the final power budget.

Choice: Option 1: MC7805CTG

Rationale: The MC7805CTG was selected because it provides the required regulated 5 V output and sufficient current capacity for the pressure-pad subsystem while maintaining additional current margin. Its through-hole TO-220 package is appropriate for manual PCB assembly. The LM2931 provides lower dropout but has less output-current capability, while the UA7805CKCS provides more current capability than the subsystem requires. The MC7805CTG therefore provides a simple and robust solution when paired with an appropriate external DC supply.

docs.title: DC Barrel Jack
docs.text:
Table 4: DC Barrel Jack Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1PJ-202ASame Sky5.5 mm OD / 2.1 mm IDThrough-Hole DC Barrel JackDigiKey Product Page * Through-hole mounting provides a strong mechanical PCB connection. 5.5 mm by 2.1 mm size is suitable for commonly available DC adapters. Right-angle orientation allows convenient access from the PCB edge. Electrical ratings provide substantial margin for the subsystem. Integrated switching contact provides additional power-routing flexibility. * Occupies more PCB area than smaller power connectors. Connecting and disconnecting the adapter applies mechanical force to the PCB. External supply must use a compatible 5.5 mm by 2.1 mm plug.* Does not inherently protect against incorrect supply voltage or polarity. Option 2PJ-102ASame Sky5.5 mm OD / 2.0 mm IDThrough-Hole DC Barrel JackDigiKey Product Page * Through-hole mounting provides good mechanical strength. Right-angle orientation is convenient for PCB-edge mounting. Electrical ratings exceed the expected subsystem requirements.* Integrated switching contact provides additional power-routing options. * 2.0 mm center pin is less compatible with common 2.1 mm plugs. Requires a specifically matched external power adapter. Occupies valuable PCB-edge space.* Does not protect the circuit from an incorrect supply voltage or polarity. Option 3PJ-002ASame Sky5.5 mm OD / 2.0 mm IDThrough-Hole DC Barrel JackDigiKey Product Page * Through-hole construction provides good mechanical strength. Electrical ratings provide substantial margin over the expected subsystem load. Right-angle configuration allows convenient PCB-edge access.* Simple construction makes schematic integration straightforward. * 2.0 mm center pin requires a matching external plug. Less compatible with common 2.1 mm adapters than the PJ-202A. Physical connector occupies significant PCB-edge space.* Does not provide protection against incorrect external supply voltage or polarity.

Choice: Option 1: PJ-202A

Rationale: The PJ-202A was selected because its through-hole construction provides a strong mechanical connection to the PCB and its right-angle orientation allows convenient access from the edge of the board. Its 5.5 mm outer diameter and 2.1 mm center-pin configuration provides a practical connection for an external DC power adapter. Its electrical ratings also provide substantial margin over the requirements of the pressure-pad subsystem. Compared with the other two options, the PJ-202A provides the preferred 2.1 mm center-pin connection for the planned external power supply.

docs.title: H-Bridge Motor Driver
docs.text:
Table 5: H-Bridge Motor Driver Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1SN754410NETexas InstrumentsQuadruple Half-H Motor Driver16-PDIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Supports motor supply voltages from 4.5 V to 36 V. Compatible with the planned 9 V motor supply. Provides up to 1 A output current per driver. Can provide bidirectional control of a brushed DC motor. Through-hole 16-PDIP package simplifies manual PCB assembly. Integrated clamp diodes provide protection when driving inductive loads. Active component with good availability. * Bipolar output stage produces a larger voltage drop than newer MOSFET-based motor drivers. Less efficient than modern MOSFET H-bridge drivers. 16-pin package occupies more PCB area than smaller motor-driver ICs.* Motor startup and stall current must remain within the driver's current limits. Option 2FAN8100NFairchild SemiconductorDual H-Bridge DC Motor Driver12-DIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Contains two H-bridge motor-driver channels. Supports forward, reverse, stop, and brake functions. Through-hole package simplifies manual PCB assembly. Compatible with microcontroller control signals. Built-in thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection.* Previously used motor-driver architecture. * 9 V is at the upper end of its recommended motor-supply range. Provides little voltage margin when used with the planned 9 V supply. Older component with more limited long-term availability.* Motor current must remain within the driver's output-current limits. Option 3L293DSTMicroelectronicsQuadruple Half-H Motor Driver16-PowerDIP Through-HoleDigiKey Product Page * Supports motor supply voltages from 4.5 V to 36 V. Compatible with the planned 9 V motor supply. Provides bidirectional brushed DC motor control. Through-hole PowerDIP package simplifies manual PCB assembly. Integrated protection diodes simplify inductive-load protection.* Commonly used motor-driver architecture. * Lower output-current capability than the SN754410NE. Bipolar output stage produces voltage drop and power loss. Provides less current margin during motor startup or stall conditions.* 16-pin package occupies additional PCB area.

Choice: Option 1: SN754410NE

Rationale: The SN754410NE was selected because it provides bidirectional control of a brushed DC motor while operating comfortably from the planned 9 V motor supply. Its 4.5 V to 36 V motor-supply range provides significantly more voltage margin than the FAN8100N, which reaches the upper end of its recommended motor-supply range at 9 V. The SN754410NE also provides greater output-current capability than the L293D. Its through-hole 16-PDIP package is appropriate for manual PCB assembly, and its integrated clamp diodes simplify protection when controlling the inductive motor load.

docs.title: DC Motor
docs.text:
Table 6: DC Motor Selection

Solution Pros Cons Option 1RF370CA-15370Mabuchi MotorBrushed DC MotorOperating Voltage: 3 V - 12 VSpeed: 5600 RPMRated Torque: 2.48 mN·mDigiKey Product Page * Operating-voltage range includes the planned 9 V motor supply. Does not require a separate motor-voltage regulator. Provides greater rated torque than the other motor options. Lower rated speed than many similar un-geared DC motors. Standard brushed DC construction allows simple H-bridge direction control. Speed can be controlled using PWM. Simple two-terminal electrical connection. * 5600 RPM is still relatively fast for direct mechanical movement. Lower output torque than a geared motor. Mechanical reduction may be required depending on the final cat-toy mechanism.* Does not include an encoder for speed or position feedback. Option 2RF500TB-12560Mabuchi MotorBrushed DC MotorOperating Voltage: 4 V - 14 VSpeed: 5500 RPMRated Torque: 1.79 mN·mDigiKey Product Page * Operating-voltage range includes the planned 9 V motor supply. Does not require a separate motor-voltage regulator. Slightly lower rated speed than the other options. Standard brushed DC motor is compatible with H-bridge direction control. Speed can be controlled using PWM.* Simple two-terminal electrical connection. * Lower rated torque than the RF370CA-15370. Larger motor body requires more mechanical installation space. 5500 RPM remains relatively fast for direct-drive movement. Does not include an encoder. Mechanical speed reduction may still be required. Option 3FK130SH-09450Mabuchi MotorBrushed DC MotorOperating Voltage: 6 V - 24 VSpeed: 7200 RPMRated Torque: 1.12 mN·mDigiKey Product Page * Operating-voltage range includes the planned 9 V motor supply. Wide operating-voltage range provides substantial voltage margin. Compact construction simplifies mechanical installation. Standard brushed DC motor is compatible with H-bridge control. Speed can be controlled using PWM.* Simple two-terminal connection. * Highest rated speed of the three options. Lowest rated torque of the three options. Lower rated power than the RF370CA-15370. Does not include an encoder. Mechanical reduction may be necessary for lower-speed operation.

Choice: Option 1: RF370CA-15370

Rationale: The RF370CA-15370 was selected because its 3 V to 12 V operating range directly includes the planned 9 V motor supply, allowing the motor to operate without an additional motor-voltage regulator. Compared with the other two options, it provides the highest rated torque while maintaining a relatively low rated speed for an un-geared DC motor. Its standard brushed DC construction allows the SN754410NE H-bridge to control motor direction, while PWM from the microcontroller can be used to control motor speed. The RF370CA-15370 therefore provides the best combination of supply-voltage compatibility, torque, speed, availability, and simple electrical integration.

Center-positive polarity matches the planned power-input configuration. Right-angle plug reduces the amount of space required behind the PCB enclosure. Universal 100 V to 240 V AC input. Level VI efficiency rating.* Active component with good DigiKey availability. * Provides more current capability than the circuit normally requires. Right-angle connector may be less convenient depending on the enclosure and barrel-jack location. Slightly more expensive than Option 2. Option 216-00134Tensility9 V / 2 A AC/DC Wall Adapter18 W5.5 mm OD / 2.1 mm ID Straight Barrel PlugDigiKey Product Page * Provides the required 9 V DC output. 2 A maximum output provides sufficient current margin for the motor and supporting electronics. 5.5 mm OD by 2.1 mm ID connector directly matches the selected PJ-202A barrel jack. Center-positive polarity matches the planned power-input configuration. Straight barrel plug provides a simple and conventional connection. Universal 100 V to 240 V AC input. Level VI efficiency rating. Active component with good DigiKey availability. Slightly less expensive than Option 1. * Straight barrel plug extends farther outward than a right-angle connector. Provides more maximum current than the circuit normally requires. External wall adapter adds to the overall system cost. Option 3WSU090-2000Triad Magnetics9 V / 2 A AC/DC Wall Adapter18 W5.5 mm OD / 2.1 mm ID Barrel PlugDigiKey Product Page * Provides the required 9 V DC output. 2 A maximum output provides sufficient current margin for the system. 5.5 mm OD by 2.1 mm ID connector matches the selected PJ-202A barrel jack. Center-positive polarity is compatible with the planned power-input configuration. Wide AC input-voltage range. Longer output cable provides additional installation flexibility. Level VI efficiency rating.* Active product with good DigiKey availability. * More expensive than the Tensility alternatives. Provides no significant electrical advantage for this application. Longer cable may be unnecessary for the subsystem.* Provides more maximum current than the circuit normally requires.

Choice: Option 2: Tensility 16-00134

Rationale: The Tensility 16-00134 was selected because it provides the required regulated 9 V DC output with a maximum current capability of 2 A, providing sufficient current margin for the DC motor and supporting electronics. Its center-positive 5.5 mm outer-diameter by 2.1 mm inner-diameter barrel connector directly matches the selected PJ-202A DC barrel jack. The straight barrel plug provides a simple and conventional connection to the subsystem. Compared with the other options, the 16-00134 provides the required electrical performance, connector compatibility, active availability, and reasonable cost without providing unnecessary power capacity.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is designed to support the pressure pad subsystem for the interactive cat toy. The FSR01CE pressure sensor detects applied pressure and produces a variable resistance that is converted into an analog voltage using a voltage divider. An MCP6004 operational amplifier buffers the sensor signal, which is then passed through a low-pass filter before being measured by the RA0 analog input of the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano.

The subsystem is powered from a 9–12 V DC input and uses an MC7805CTG linear voltage regulator to provide a regulated 5 V supply. The schematic also includes a debugging LED, a debounced pushbutton, test points, spare GPIO connections, and an 8-pin ribbon cable interface for communication with the other subsystems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A power budget was created for the pressure pad subsystem to determine the maximum current required by the electrical components. The subsystem uses an ALT-0601 AC/DC adapter with an output of 6 VDC at 1 A as its external power source.

The power budget includes the PIC18F57Q10 microcontroller, MCP6004 operational amplifier, FSR01CE pressure pad sensor, and indicator LED. A 25% safety margin was included to ensure sufficient current is available for the subsystem.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text: The completed power budget shows the expected power requirements of the pressure pad subsystem. The calculated current requirements, including the 25% safety margin, are within the available current capacity of the power source. The ALT-0601 AC/DC adapter provides 6 VDC at a maximum of 1 A, providing sufficient current for the subsystem.
